Ivy: quick accessibility review from today's dashboard QA — filter chips area has a few keyboard + SR issues. filing here so we can group fixes. Rohit: thanks. summary bullets pls? Ivy: quick list: 1) chips are focusable but use role=button; SR reads names OK but when you remove a chip with Delete key VO reads the removed chip and then immediately re-reads the toolbar label (noisy). 2) removal via Backspace when focus is on the chip doesn't work consistently across browsers. 3) visual focus style for chips is subtle and gets lost on dark theme. 4) no aria-live for aggregated filter summary, so SR users miss counts after large multi-filter changes. Sofia: can you paste sample markup? curious about roles/aria. Ivy: gist: ```
``` Removal is implemented by removing the button node from DOM, then updating a small summary text elsewhere (but summary update isn't announced). Ben: pattern notes: chips as buttons are fine, but deleting the focused element can create SR race where the act of removing the node causes screen reader to fall back and re-announce nearby landmarks. We should restore focus properly and announce the removal succinctly. Rohit: recommended behavior: when a chip is removed while focused, move focus to the next chip if present, otherwise to the previous chip, or finally to the "clear filters" control. use a polite live region (outside the chip container) to announce "Removed filter: Type: production. 3 filters remaining" — update this after focus move. support both Delete and Backspace for removal and surface a11y-friendly tooltip or aria-keyshortcuts for keyboard help. ensure chip elements have accessible names that include the text and removal affordance e.g., `aria-label="Type: production. Press Delete to remove"` (but consider verbosity tradeoffs). Sofia: small nuance: avoid putting the live region inside the chip container (same re-render problem). Also prefer announcing concise messages, not full visible text when it's long. For long filter values, use truncated visible text but announce full value in the live update. Ivy: good catch. also found a weird focus order when using keyboard to tab from search input into chips — focus sometimes jumps to Clear All button instead of the first chip. probably because chips are dynamically re-rendered and tabindex ordering not stable. Ben: fix for that: maintain DOM order for chips (append/remove rather than re-render entire list). keep a roving tabindex pattern if we want arrow navigation (set only one chip tabindex=0).
